examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: S'asseoir sur une chaise. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to sit down, to seat'.
Transitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to sit down, to seat'.

examples.trans: A cushion to sit down on.

examples.text: Tu dois te balader avec un coussin pour t'asseoir.

meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.note: Très bien = very well, fine. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

meanings.note: bien sûr que + sentence = of course...

meanings.note: the standard greeting until evening

meanings.note: Changer quelque chose. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to change'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'changé').

le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film

French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'must, to have to'.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced. French conjunction meaning 'and', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le garçon', plural 'les garçons') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'boy'.

examples.trans: Not bad. I play a boy who has a broken heart.

meanings.note: The h is silent: l'homme. Masculine noun ('le homme', plural 'les hommes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'man'.
In general statements. Masculine noun ('le homme', plural 'les hommes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'man'.

examples.text: Le rôle est pour un homme.
examples.trans: The part is for a man.

examples.text: Ils ont pensé que ce serait mieux avec un homme.
examples.trans: They thought it would be better with a man.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?

meanings.note: Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Il ne répond jamais au téléphone pendant le week-end.
examples.trans: He never answers the phone during the weekend.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: Adverb: je veux juste. Invariable French adverb meaning 'just'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Adjective. Invariable French adverb meaning 'just'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.

Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to occupy'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'occupé').

meanings.note: Si tu veux = if you want. French conjunction meaning 'if', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
